skill.name: better-layout
skill.description: Helps with grouping, alignment, reading order, responsive structure and room for translated text, so a layout holds up when it is resized, translated or mirrored.
skill.summary: Review and improve interface grouping, alignment, spacing, responsive behavior, and layouts for translated text and right-to-left languages.

content.user_title: Improve Responsive Layouts and Reading Order
content.value_statement: Interface layouts can lose clarity or clip content when resized, translated, or mirrored. This skill guides focused fixes for grouping, alignment, spacing, and responsive structure.
actual_capabilities: Review grouping, shared alignment edges, control distinction, and reading order against visible layout failures.
Recommend logical CSS properties and direction-specific adjustments for right-to-left interfaces.
Identify grid and flex overflow, fixed-size text clipping, and unsuitable responsive breakpoints.
Suggest safe-area insets, sticky-header scroll offsets, and visible cues for hidden content.
Guide checks at supported widths, 320 pixels, 200 percent zoom, and with expanded translated strings.
Report layout findings by principle and severity, with source locations, proposed changes, user impact, and verification gaps.
limitations: The skill provides guidance and examples, not an executable scanner or bundled browser-testing tool.
Rendered verification requires browser access; unavailable checks must remain marked as not verified.
It does not replace reviews of focus behavior, target sizes, typography, wording, color, or animation.
Default spacing values are starting points, not requirements that override an established project design system.

use_cases.title: Repair Responsive Components
use_cases.description: Find overflow, clipped actions, and unsuitable breakpoints in components used across different container widths.

use_cases.title: Improve Interface Hierarchy
use_cases.description: Review grouping, shared edges, control distinction, and primary actions while preserving existing spacing tokens.

use_cases.title: Prepare Layouts for Localization
use_cases.description: Check long translated labels, wrapping, right-to-left mirroring, and safe-area positioning before a multilingual release.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Single View
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this view for grouping, alignment, and reading order. Identify visible failures and suggest small changes using existing spacing tokens.

prompt_templates.title: Fix Responsive Overflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this component at supported widths and 320 pixels. Find overflow or clipped actions, propose focused fixes, and mark unavailable checks as not verified.

prompt_templates.title: Check Translation and Mirroring
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this layout with expanded labels, German text, and right-to-left direction. Preserve DOM order and identify clipping, broken mirroring, or missing disclosure cues.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Complete Layout
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit these views using project tokens. Check supported widths, 320 pixels, 200 percent zoom, RTL, sticky headers, and safe areas. Group findings by principle.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: review multiple views and report verification coverage.

output_examples.input: A settings form uses identical gaps within and between sections, plus separator lines after every field.
output: Medium: section boundaries are unclear because all spacing is equal.
Use the existing spacing scale to make gaps between groups at least twice the gaps within each group.
Remove separators where spacing already communicates the grouping.
Rendered verification: not verified without browser access.

output_examples.input: A right-to-left interface keeps a floating action on the physical right, while a long translated button label clips.
output: Medium: the floating action does not mirror with the interface.
Pair physical positioning with matching safe-area insets and add a right-to-left override.
High when the clipped label blocks an action: allow the button to grow and the action row to wrap.
Verify the RTL view, expanded labels, supported widths, and 200 percent zoom.

best_practices: Provide the relevant components, supported widths, and existing spacing or density tokens before requesting a review.
Require a demonstrable failure and user impact for each finding, rather than treating different spacing values as defects.
Verify changes with narrow widths, zoom, expanded translations, and RTL; explicitly record checks that could not run.
anti_patterns: Replace established spacing tokens with default measurements without evidence of a layout failure.
Change visual order independently of DOM order to hide reading-order problems.
Approve uninspected views or claim browser verification when only source files were reviewed.

faq.question: What does this skill review?
faq.answer: It reviews grouping, alignment, reading order, spacing, responsive structure, translated-text growth, and right-to-left layout behavior.

faq.question: Which AI tools are supported?
faq.answer: The marketplace lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. Browser verification depends on the tools available in your environment.

faq.question: Does it run an automated layout scanner?
faq.answer: No. The package contains written guidance and CSS or HTML examples, not an executable scanner.

faq.question: Will it replace my design system?
faq.answer: No. Fixes should use your project styling system and spacing tokens. Default measurements apply only when no established scale exists.

faq.question: Can it verify layouts without a browser?
faq.answer: It can inspect source structure, sizing rules, and logical properties. Rendered checks that cannot run must be reported as not verified.

faq.question: Does it provide a complete accessibility audit?
faq.answer: No. It addresses layout-related visibility and reading order. Focus behavior, target sizes, and other accessibility concerns require a separate review.
